Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by City of Claremont Councilmember, Ed Reece.

The Invocation was led by Pastor James Mendoza, Altar Foursquare Church.

CLOSED SESSION

Interim City Attorney Casso announced that, for Closed Session Item No. 1, direction was provided to the City
Negotiator and there was no reportable action.

CEREMONIAL

Presentation of Certificate of Recognition to Michael “Shan” Thompson, Facilities Supervisor, for 43 years of
service to the City of Azusa

Mayor Gonzales presented a Certificate of Recognition to Facilities Supervisor Thompson.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Venerable Nicholas Thanissaro, from the Dhammakaya Meditation Center, invited the community to attend an
outdoor Full Moon Meditation event scheduled for November 5, 2025.

Yasmin Eastwood shared concerns regarding her property and expressed her appreciation for first responders.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

SGVCOG President Introduction

SGVCOG President and City of Claremont Councilmember, Ed Reece, provided a brief presentation
highlighting the significance of the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) and its
relationships with member cities; shared recent achievements, highlighted partnerships with the City of Azusa
including project management, compliance support, and regional planning efforts; and introduced the launch of
the “I Heart SGV” program.

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez reported on Closed Session Item No. 2, stating that Staff provided information to the
City Council, there was no reportable action, and Staff was given direction.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez announced that Community Resources will host a “Fall Into Wellness Fair” on
November 6 at Memorial Park; shared that he recently toured the Flyer manufacturing plant in Alabama, which
produces CNG and hydrogen fuel buses; and invited the community to attend the Veterans Day Celebration on
November 11 at 11:00 a.m., in front of City Hall.

Councilmember Avila announced that the Cruising Back to Route 66 Car Show will take place on November 9
in Downtown Azusa; noted that the Azusa City Library will host “Family Picnic Bingo” on November 13; and
congratulated Community Resources Staff on their successful Day of the Dead event.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
November 3, 2025
 Councilmember Mendez announced that Fadi’s Flowers will host a workshop on November 12; shared that
E.S.L. tutoring will be offered at Azusa High School on December 10; congratulated Staff on the Día de los
Muertos event; and congratulated the Los Angeles community on the Los Angeles Dodgers 2nd World Series
Championship.

Councilmember Bow announced that E.S.L. tutoring will be held at the Neighborhood Homework House,
located at the former Center Middle School, beginning October 28 through December 9; announced the K-Pop
Demon Hunter “Family Craft Hour” at the Azusa City Library on November 20; and highlighted local food
pantries and food banks that are available for the community in need.

Mayor Gonzales announced that a significant sewer rate adjustment will impact the community and stated that a
rate adjustment vote will be made available to the community in 2026; requested that the previously tabled
fireworks item from a prior meeting be brought back for consideration and placed on the agenda for the next
meeting for an official vote to which there was no support from the Council.

City Clerk Cornejo announced that there are two vacancies on the Arts, Cultural & Historic Preservation
Commission; explained that both are partial terms, with one term expiring on September 30, 2026, and the other
expiring on September 30, 2029; stated that the City Clerk’s Office will be reaching out to previous applicants
who had expressed interest ; and noted that applications for these positions will be accepted at the City Clerk’s
Office through November 13.
